sections.COMMENTS:
This composite source straddles the inner part of the Molise region, across the high Trigno R. valley, northeast of the city of Iserrnia, and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is a near-vertical, ca. N-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a virtual lack of seismicity in this region. However, the zone falls within one of the mesoseismal areas of the catastrophic 5-30 Dec 1456 (Mw 7.0 and 6.6, respectively) multiple earthquake, that has affected a large portion of southern Italy. Given (1) the exceptional extents of the damage area, (2) the presence of at least 2/3 sub-regions where effects were maximum, and (3) the puzzling distance among these sub-regions, as of today historical catalogs have concentrated these events in two main sub-events, their epicenters falling approximately along the axis of the southern Apennines. However, this multiple earthquake holds several complexities that have been thoroughly addressed only in recent years, concerning at least the elusive damage distribution and the historical sources that firmly document it â€“ a task only complicated by the old age of the latter ones. All the more challenging is to explain the possible tectonic mechanism that has caused such unusually broad, seemingly contemporaneous peak destruction in areas (and even tectonic provinces) remarkably far away from one another. For an in-depth description of the 1456 seismic crisis, studied here and elsewhere in this Database, the reader can refer to Guidoboni and Comastri (2005), and Fracassi and Valensise (2007), and rererences therein.
This Source is thought to be the westernmost strand of the ca. E-W trending, strike-slip, right-lateral fault system of the Molise 2002 and Mattinata Fault. Such E-W trending tectonic mechanism seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. Field evidence in the area is scarce, although seismological data in the au-large region (including the hypocenters of the Molise 2002 earthquakes, just east of this source) suggest the presence of a deep-seated (rooting at ca. 25 km), blind structure that has been associated with one mainshock of the 1456 sequence. To the west, this source borders the shallower, NW-SE trending, main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
The main segment of this Source has been associated with one sub-event of the 1456 sequence. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the regional sub-surface structures. The dip was based on geological and geometrical considerations. The rake represents oblique, right-lateral strike slip, based on geological and seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. The slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
